svg.text: Feedback / forwarded data to an earlier stage
Input left open: tied to 0, never needed
Dots are junctions; plain crossings are not connected.
IF_ID, ID_EX, EX_MEM, MEM_WB use reg_n_sf / dffg_sf; PC uses pc_reg_sf.
WE = (not stall) or flush. D = flush ? FLUSH_VAL : D. Flush wins.
FLUSH_VAL: 0 for control and data, x"00000013" (nop) for instructions.
PC stalls on s_Halt or s_PC_stall (G_PC_STALL, org2).
Open inputs (o) are tied to 0: ID_EX stall, PC flush and all of
EX_MEM / MEM_WB never need to stall or flush.
Load-use: a load in EX whose rd the instruction in ID reads in EX
(store data excluded) -> stall PC and IF_ID, flush ID_EX (1 bubble).
-> flush IF_ID and ID_EX (the 2 wrong-path instructions), no stall.
ID_EX_flush = load_use + ctrl_taken; the two never occur together.
Units are in src/Hazard and wired into RISCV_Processor.vhd.
10 = s_fwd_MEM (EX/MEM). EX/MEM wins when both match.
A load in EX/MEM is never forwarded (its data is not ready).
FWD_M: store data = s_RegWrData when MEM/WB writes the store rs2.
G_REG_CLK writes REGS on the falling edge, so WB -> ID needs nothing.
Branch, jal, jalr resolve in EX. No prediction (keeps fetching PC+4),
no delay slots. Fetch_Ctrl_IF loads the target at the end of EX.
Taken branch / jal / jalr: 2-cycle penalty. Not-taken branch: 0.
Flushed slots become nop with all control bits 0 (no writes, no halt).
wfi: s_Halt (WB) stalls the PC through G_PC_STALL; no flush needed.
EX_MEM still stores pcsrc, add2out, jump, jumpreg; MEM does not use them.
